analysis: The closest integrates mathematics, probability, programming, data, econometrics, algorithms and optimisation around microeconomic, macroeconomic, public-policy and financial-appraisal questions. Its courses have specific complementary functions; the substantial response is not inferred from a broad quantitative label. Dedicated advanced proofs, econometric asymptotics and actuarial specialisms remain explicit limitations.

Business analytics changes priorities to software, relational data, machine learning and neural prediction with AI ethics and actual business/economic effects. The financial alternative changes priorities to accounting, startup finance/planning, banking/markets and behavioural choices with economic, mathematical and empirical tools. It is a bounded finance response, not full specialist quantitative-finance training. Pairwise differences of 37.5, 30 and 60 EC each way satisfy the numerical floor and change actual academic purposes.

All thirty-two selected courses were considered from their current profiles or available descriptions. Description-only econometrics receives full OLS/GLS/IV, tests, Stata/Monte Carlo and empirical-paper consideration and is aligned to introductory econometrics, not discarded or overstated as advanced GMM/ML. Description-only advanced calculus, databases and behavioural economics receive their actual multivariable/ODE, SQL and experimental-bias scope. No missing profile is used as absence of relevance.

Money and Banking has substantial financial-market and institutional content, including contracts and risk, interest rates, banks and simulated balance-sheet decisions; it is not dismissed as personal finance. Accounting supplies discounted investment appraisal and control. Business gateway supplies specific funding/business-plan context and the formal banking prerequisite. Business/AI is economic and institutional analysis, not technical learning algorithms. General Ethics supplies moral reasoning but is not a match to historical economic thinkers.

Four original offering conflicts are resolved through rescheduling with the same course sets. All three plans have twenty-four unique courses, four per covered semester, 180 EC, first-year PPD and at least six advanced courses. Formal prerequisites precede dependants. Data preparation precedes machine learning; ML precedes deep learning, research methods precede behavioural statistics and econometrics, and algorithms precedes advanced algorithms. No old offering or unsupported extra term is restored.

Twenty-one partial placements and ten dedicated gaps cover each external unit and selected UCR course once. SQL is a real component of computational econometrics but not all of it; numerical ODE/integration relates to analytical differentiation/integration with a specific method limitation. Public economics and Policy Analysis share actual policy-model/evidence inquiry, while the latter’s dedicated causal and dynamic methods are not attributed to UCR. Behavioural economics addresses the actual reasoning-bias part of Philosophy of Science and Statistics; broader philosophy remains outside that relationship. Advanced econometrics, insurance, separate game theory/auctions, history of thought, the society lab and individual thesis remain explicit gaps. Optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI

DISARIN311.name: Optimization Methods in AI

DISARIN312.name: Reinforcement Learning

DISCOMP212.name: Database Management Systems

DISCOMP213.name: Software Development

alignment.rationale: Both develop reflective competence assessment, learning goals and academic/professional choices. UCR also includes civic engagement, academic writing and collaborative inquiry.

Both evaluate financial investments using discounting and quantitative appraisal. UCR adds accounting and corporate budgeting; Tilburg also develops insurance, pension and stochastic financial models.

Both examine pricing and risk of financial contracts. Tilburg adds CAPM/factor models and econometric asset-return analysis; UCR combines market pricing with banks, monetary policy and balance-sheet risk decisions.

Both use formal models of consumers, production, market structure and allocation. UCR also introduces macroeconomics; Tilburg emphasises explicit solutions and additional uncertainty/information problems.
Both use economic models to study output, inflation, employment, growth and policy, including international relationships. The mathematical treatment and applications differ.

Both analyse strategic market behaviour, competition and economic choice through formal models. Tilburg concentrates on normal/extensive-form games, spatial/dynamic competition and entry; UCR spans wider microeconomic topics.

Both evaluate economic policy with models and empirical evidence. UCR centres efficiency, equity, tax and public-expenditure questions; Tilburg develops dedicated micro-causal identification and dynamic macroeconometric methods.

Both develop regression estimation and instrumental-variable methods with empirical economic applications in Stata. Tilburg derives more finite-sample and asymptotic properties; UCR additionally emphasises GLS, tests and Monte Carlo illustration.

Both examine reasoning biases and departures from rational economic choice. UCR develops behavioural economic models and experiments; Tilburg additionally investigates scientific method, probability interpretations and the evidence supplied by statistical models.

Both use probabilistic and Markov-style models for uncertainty. UCR concentrates on beliefs and sequential decisions; Tilburg develops Markov and branching processes, queues, inventory and service-operation models.
Both develop elementary mathematical proof, including induction and contradiction. UCR centres logic and discrete structures; Tilburg also reviews algebra, differentiation and integration.

Both formulate and solve constrained linear/discrete optimisation problems. Tilburg develops simplex, duality, shadow prices, branch-and-bound and cuts; UCR places linear/discrete optimisation in a broader search and AI toolkit.

Both study relational data models and SQL. Tilburg combines that module with Python data processing and scientific computing for econometrics; UCR develops relational database management more specifically.

Both study greedy and dynamic programming, network-flow/optimisation algorithms and their performance. Tilburg additionally centres routing, scheduling, integer formulations and approximation quality.
Both introduce Python, data collections, recursion, object-oriented programming and computational problem solving.

Both study single-variable limits, differentiation, integration and series. Tilburg emphasises mathematical theorems and proofs; UCR develops analytical/computational techniques and dynamic-model applications.
Both study linear systems, vectors, matrices, spaces and transformations. Their mix of proof, computational methods and applications differs.

Both solve differential-equation and integration problems. UCR centres numerical approximation, algorithms, stability and error; Tilburg centres analytical linear systems, convergence, measures and Riemann/Stieltjes/Lebesgue integration.

Both extend calculus to functions of several variables for quantitative modelling. Tilburg develops the mathematical theory and proofs; UCR includes differential equations and computer-algebra applications.

Both develop multivariate probability, estimation, confidence intervals and simulation. Tilburg emphasises limit theorems and estimator properties; UCR additionally includes Bayesian reasoning and sampling algorithms.

Both select, apply and interpret statistical procedures and uncertainty. Tilburg develops estimator, confidence-interval, testing and nonparametric theory; UCR uses behavioural data, experimental design and multivariable models.
Mathematical probability is developed in the course aligned to the separate Probability and Statistics unit; it is not counted twice.
The selected linear algebra course is placed with the first dedicated unit; no second selected course reproduces the additional proof-based advanced linear-algebra sequence.
Academic writing and presentation support the selected courses, but none is counted again as this separate EOR communication-skills unit.

The selected econometrics course is placed with the stronger introductory OLS/IV/Stata relationship. No additional course supplies this separate nonlinear, GMM, maximum-likelihood and asymptotic-theory sequence.
Selected courses include empirical and computational projects, but none is counted again as the separate integrated EOR society-lab requirement.
Probability, learning and financial evidence provide relevant foundations, but no selected course centres insurance-portfolio pricing, credibility and claims reserving.
Strategic choices and discrete reasoning appear in selected courses, but none is counted again as the dedicated non-cooperative/cooperative economic-game theory unit.
No selected course centres axiomatic bargaining, auction equilibria, Shapley values and network power.
General ethical reasoning complements normative reflection, but no selected course centres the historical development and ethical assumptions of economic thought.
The independent econometric or operations-research thesis remains compulsory. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.
